when a photo or any file is deleted, the pointer will no longer be pointing to that perticular location in the memory but the content will still be present, but the data in that location can still be overridden (meaning replacing with new data). once the data is overridden you cant recover the old data that was present there. this is how storage works.
There is no concept of deletion of data, just data wont be pointed or data will be overridden.

content: What the hell is he/she talking about, ever single thing we store in our system it take space in our rom as we all know, and let suppose you deleted some file then what would happen ? Guess ? Well the area where you stored your file will become free means kernal will tell os that "bro now start showing extra space in the UI" so that user would think ok now i got back my 1 GB space after deleting file, but the thing is your file is still there, but now your os know that if you download any file then that file re-write a area where your first file was stored, so it means if you delete something and after that if you don't do anything that re-writes the data you can still retrieve it, and it is possible using some software (you can google search for this). But if you do any activity that re-writes that area(like downloading something) then it is impossible to retrive deleted data. So in short "delete karne jaesi cheej hoti hai" don't listen to these morons.

I always screen record mostly minecraft gameplay to edit and put on YouTube. Normally it wouldn't be a problem since I need to upload videos to grow as a YouTuber. content:
I honestly don’t understand what the problem with cloud storage is. It’s incredibly useful, especially when your device unexpectedly gets lost, stolen, or simply breaks. You still have all your photos and other data safely stored.
And believe me, I learned that lesson the hard way.
Besides that, Google Photos isn’t really any different from Apple’s iCloud Photos when it comes to the basic idea. In the end, the cost is pretty much the same, and Google Photos actually offers some really nice and useful features.

The days of keeping all your music and thousands of photos stored exclusively on your device are definitely over. At least for me, that’s not an option anymore.

And honestly, those one or two euros a month aren’t going to hurt anyone. For the peace of mind and convenience you get in return, it’s absolutely worth it.

Yes, Apple has a very simple way to copy everything at once!
At the bottom of your Photos app, tap to select the first image or video. Then tap at the very top of your iPhone screen — the app will automatically scroll all the way up to the top of your album. Everything in your Photos app will now be highlighted in blue, and you can copy it all!

Note: If you have, for example, 20,000 photos and videos, you should split this process into smaller sections; otherwise, the app might crash. Good luck!

Also, people don’t have “Androids” — they have Android-based devices. Anyone in tech should know that Android is the software, while Samsung (for example) is the hardware.

content: So I'm an amateur videographer. Each time I do an event, I would upload the footage to my Google Drive and then share it with the client. And after leaving the footage on my Drive for over a month I delete it and very next day the client wants to know where it went. So, I came up with a new system. Each time I do an event, I make a new Google account (sometimes two) based on the name of the event or the client, and upload the footage to that Drive. I then share the username and password with the client giving them full control of the account to do what they want with. Now the footage is not taking up my space nor the client's space and can stay there for eternity (or until Google decides to remove unused accounts etc...) I think it's a pretty smart idea.

content: Good plan Neil, but with one small catch! When you set up a new account and tell it to backup your photos, it will backup ALL the photos that are stored on your phone, not just the most recent year, which could mean several year's worth, so you'll be in the same position you were when you started. If you want an account for each year, for example, you'd need to make sure your phone ONLY had this year's photos on it. Then you'd need to delete them all from your phone before starting a new account for the next year. Also beware some services sync rather than backup, which means when you delete on your phone, it deletes them online too. The moral being to always backup photos onto a separate physical drive somewhere before doing anything clever!

What Is Mouth Larva?
A larva is an insect that’s hatched from an egg but hasn’t developed wings yet. Mouth larva usually comes from certain fly species that invade soft tissues inside the oral cavity, such as gums and open wounds. These pests typically infect livestock and other vertebrate animals in tropical areas, but they can affect humans in rare cases. People can get oral myiasis by eating foods containing larvae. Flies can also enter the mouth and lay eggs in wounds.

1. Go to _My Files_
2. Go to _Manage Storage_

Probably some differences based on what type of file you downloaded.
